title: Conformal soft modes at elastic instabilities
authors: Lars Franke, Nick Sander, Markus Garst
abstract: In case a crystal is close to a continuous elastic phase transition, pronounced critical fluctuations emerge. We show that on the level of linear elasticity theory the displacement vector for these critical modes obeys a condition reminiscent of the conformal Killing equation. For an isostructural instability, four critical modes arise corresponding to one dilation and three special conformal transformations. At crystal symmetry-breaking instabilities, the critical fluctuations include a continuum of modes even for crystals with finite size. For certain cases, these comprise the conformal transformations associated with two-dimensional Minkowski space. These results have implications for critical elastic phenomena as well as for extremal mechanical metamaterials.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the critical fluctuations in crystals near elastic phase transitions by analyzing the zero modes of the displacement field. It shows that these soft modes obey conditions related to conformal symmetries, identifying specific modes like dilation and special conformal transformations depending on the type of instability. This provides a powerful mathematical framework for understanding critical elastic phenomena.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the nature of critical fluctuations and zero modes in crystals approaching continuous elastic phase transitions (elastic instabilities). It seeks to characterize the associated soft modes using linear elasticity theory.
main_result: The critical fluctuations are governed by conditions reminiscent of the conformal Killing equation, leading to specific zero modes: one dilation mode and three special conformal transformation modes for isostructural instabilities, and conformal transformations of 2D Minkowski space for symmetry-breaking instabilities.
method: The analysis uses linear elasticity theory, deriving zero mode conditions from the vanishing internal stress ($	ext{C}\Gamma = 0$) and classifying instabilities based on the vanishing eigenmoduli of the elasticity tensor.
model_or_system: The system is crystalline matter near an elastic instability. The theory is built upon the displacement vector $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})$ and the elastic energy density $W$, analyzed via the strain tensor $\varepsilon_{ij}$.
key_observables: Zero mode displacement field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x})$, elastic eigenmoduli, principal strains ($\varepsilon_{\alpha ij}$), and the resulting conformal transformations.
important_parameters: The nature of the instability (isostructural vs. symmetry-breaking), the dimensionality of the critical subspace, and the elastic constants $C_{ijkl}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to linear elasticity theory and assumes the absence of external stresses; the zero mode condition (vanishing internal stress) is shown to be necessary.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate macroscopic zero modes for both the volumetric singlet (showing Dilation and SCT) and at a symmetry-breaking instability, demonstrating the physical manifestation of the derived mathematical modes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the zero mode condition from the vanishing internal stress, classifying instabilities based on the resulting strain subspace ($\Gamma$), and then deriving the specific mathematical forms of the zero modes (conformal Killing/Minkowski transformations) associated with different types of instability.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between critical elastic fluctuations and conformal symmetries (conformal Killing equations) provides a deep mathematical structure to mechanical phase transitions, which is relevant for understanding emergent symmetries in condensed matter systems.
